principles.title: Money is integer arithmetic
principles.body: Currency does not survive floating point, and a shared bill is only trustworthy when every participant's device computes the same figure. Amounts are held and split as integer minor units under their ISO 4217 exponent, with the leftover cent distributed deterministically rather than rounded out of existence.
principles.exampleDetail: A cent-exact ISO 4217 multi-currency ledger, split by largest remainder — RM51.50 across four people resolves to RM12.875 before the remainder is assigned, not after.
principles.evidence: resume.txt lines 27-28; the RM51.50 ÷ 4 largest-remainder diagram is assets/split.svg in the public Bupples-showcase repository (smaller-projects.md §4).

principles.title: Trust the server, not the client
principles.body: Anything a client can compute, a client can also lie about. The writes that decide who owes whom run in Cloud Functions and are idempotent, so a retried request cannot double a debt, and everything else is bounded by Firestore Security Rules, which are what actually hold. App Check is integrated on the client, but enforcement across the callables is still switched off in source, so it is not yet a layer I claim.
principles.exampleDetail: Idempotent Cloud Functions behind Firestore Security Rules, with Remote Config. App Check integrated; enforcement pending.

principles.title: Launch is the start of the work
principles.body: A store listing is a commitment to keep shipping, not a finish line — the interesting version of a product is the one that survives its first month of real use.
principles.exampleDetail: First released 2 July 2026; version 1.2.5 reached the App Store on 27 July 2026.

principles.title: Reliability claims need a test behind them
principles.body: "It works" describes one run, not a system. Adelante's content pipeline — caching, deduplication, quality scoring, strict filtering — is covered by automated tests because a scheduled pipeline fails quietly, and the failure shows up on someone's Lock Screen rather than in a crash report.
principles.exampleDetail: 117 Dart unit tests over the client's content layer — library loading, deduplication, strict filtering, quality floor and refresh policy — with widget payload parity covered alongside.
principles.evidence: Counted in the Adelante repo: grep -rahE "^[[:space:]]*(test|testWidgets)\\(" test/*.dart | wc -l -> 117, across 18 files. All 117 are Dart flutter_test client tests: find functions -name '*test*' -not -path '*/node_modules/*' returns nothing, so the TypeScript package holding the two onSchedule handlers has no tests — which is why this example no longer attributes them to the Cloud Functions layer. 58 of the 117 sit in content-pipeline files; the rest are widget parity/payload, search, preferences and native-source checks. The résumé, the showcase README and ARCHITECTURE.md all still say ~80 and are stale — see CONTENT_GAPS.md §2.5.

principles.title: Keep private data on the device
principles.body: The safest place for a camera frame is the machine that captured it. Photoshoot runs its entire pipeline locally — Electron with context isolation, sandboxing and a strict CSP, WebGL2 for the effects, MediaPipe for face tracking — so nothing is uploaded in order to be processed.
principles.exampleDetail: Local-first Electron/WebGL2 architecture; camera processing and captures stay on-device, with Firebase Hosting serving only the app itself.

principles.title: Go native where the platform is the product
principles.body: Cross-platform tooling is a default, not a rule. When the product surface is a widget rather than a screen, the framework has nothing to render into, so the widget gets written twice — properly — in the platform's own toolkit.
principles.exampleDetail: WidgetKit/SwiftUI on iOS and Android RemoteViews on Android, for Home Screen, Lock Screen and StandBy, over a shared Flutter app.
principles.evidence: resume.txt lines 29-31; the adelante-showcase README states "the main product isn't a feed or a dashboard — it's the widgets" (smaller-projects.md §4).

archive.name: Tajweed
archive.blurb: A Quranic recitation platform that paints tajweed rules into the script itself, so a learner sees a rule before having to remember it. Working inside another developer's Next.js codebase, I rebuilt the navigation and information architecture around a staged learning path, replaced a progress model that returned unlocked for every lesson with real gating, and added the model layer test-first — the repository had no test harness before. The recitation reader, the speech analysis and the curriculum already existed and stayed.
archive.role: Collaborator on someone else's product — 15 of the repository's 31 commits; the redesign branch was merged to main on 20 June 2026, changing 51 files.
archive.why: The deployed site is the only public evidence there is: the repository belongs to its owner and is private, so there is no code link to offer.
archive.evidence: smaller-projects.md §1. Remote is github.com/HatemSamad/Tajweed, private (gh api returns private: true; unauthenticated fetch 404s). Authorship 16/15 across 31 commits. Merge commit 57a67cb, 2026-06-20, authored by Yousof Selim; git diff --shortstat 3c72c02..50788ed = 51 files, +5,034/-1,216. Stack read from web/package.json: Next.js 16.2.7, React 19.2.4, TypeScript 5, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui, Zustand 5.0.14, Vitest 2.1.9. Tests: 5 Vitest files, 43 it() cases; commit f65cbf2 "Add Vitest test harness" proves none existed before. The isUnlocked: () => true before/after is documented in the same section. Live URL verified reachable (title "Tajweed — Learn"). NOTE: the résumé and the current site date this "Sep 2025 — Present"; git shows the repository's first commit on 2026-02-06 and Yousof's earliest on 2026-02-10, so the year here follows git and needs owner confirmation.

archive.name: Fallen Asteri
archive.blurb: A stamina-based souls-like where you grow stronger by beating the enemy in front of you, built in Godot by three people between April and June 2024 and released on itch.io. My share was the level and camera work across the game's scenes, player and boss sprite animation, the title, pause, options and death screens with the health and stamina HUD, and combat tuning — hitboxes, slash timing, and a life-steal system on kill.
archive.role: One of three contributors — 179 of 491 commits. I created the repository and set up the branch-and-PR workflow the team worked through; 37 of its 102 pull-request merges are mine.
archive.why: The first thing built with other people: roughly a hundred feature branches merged through one repository, and a public release at the end of it.
archive.evidence: smaller-projects.md §2. gh api repos/yeegz/Fallen-Asteri: public, not a fork, GDScript 100%, created 2024-04-04, pushed 2024-06-20 — the résumé's Apr–Jun 2024 is exact. Contributors: The-silver-ghost 251, yeegz 179, Yoshenan 58 (491 total). Merge authorship re-derived 2026-07-29 from a fresh clone: git log --format="%an|%s" | grep "Merge pull request" -> 102 pull-request merges on HEAD, Sanjeevan A/L Rames 52, Yousof Selim 37, Yoshenan 13 — his teammate merged more than he did, so no lead title is claimed. Per-file blame at pre-reorg tree 27c339a. itch.io page verified live: Godot, HTML5, Released, tags Fighting/Platformer/Souls-like. Source repository is public at github.com/yeegz/Fallen-Asteri (the archive shape carries one href, so the playable build is linked here). IMPORTANT: the résumé line "implemented player movement, combat, and scene transitions" is not supported — he has zero commits on scene_transition.gd, 15 of 92 on the player controller and 5 of 48 on the enemy script.
